scope.included: Deterministic fixed-orbit results for {b^n*x}, especially b=10, and digit-complexity or irrationality-measure hypotheses that can be compared with a proved property of pi.
excluded: Every source already retained by T4.
General almost-everywhere, full-measure, Hausdorff-dimension, and probabilistic shrinking-target results.
Finite computations of digits of pi.
Results only for non-integral multipliers p/q with q >= 2, except as screened exclusions.
Constructed normal numbers unless they provide a deterministic obstruction to an arithmetic hypothesis proposed for pi.

screened_exclusions.citation: L. Flatto, J. C. Lagarias, A. Pollington, On the range of fractional parts {xi(p/q)^n}, Acta Arith. 70 (1995), 125-147
screened_exclusions.reason: Its stated theorems assume coprime p > q >= 2, so they do not specialize to the integer multiplier 10 (q=1).

screened_exclusions.citation: Y. Bugeaud, Linear mod one transformations and the distribution of fractional parts {xi(p/q)^n}, Acta Arith. 114 (2004), 301-311
screened_exclusions.reason: The multiplier is again non-integral p/q with q >= 2; its full-measure assertions in the interval parameter are also not fixed-pi conclusions.

screened_exclusions.citation: A. Dubickas, Powers of a rational number modulo 1 cannot lie in a small interval, Acta Arith. 137 (2009), 233-247
screened_exclusions.reason: Theorem 1 assumes 1 < q < p < q^2 and therefore excludes q=1 and multiplier 10.

screened_exclusions.citation: E. Stefanescu, The dispersion of dilated lacunary sequences, with applications in multiplicative Diophantine approximation, Adv. Math. 463 (2025), 110062
screened_exclusions.reason: The abstract's logarithmic dispersion conclusion is for existence of a dilation factor and its second bound is for Lebesgue-almost all factors, not the named factor pi.

retrieval_notes: The first Kwon publisher download endpoint failed with TLS errors; the Crossref-deposited ocean.kisti.re.kr URL succeeded and is pinned.
The first Salikhov MathNet request returned HTTP 403; replay requires the recorded User-Agent and Referer headers.
The irrationality-complexity Crossref request initially returned HTTP 429 and succeeded on the recorded retry.
An initially retrieved Zeilberger-Zudilin paper concerned logarithms rather than pi and was removed from the retained corpus rather than misclassified as pi evidence.
limitations: This is a dated finite corpus, not an exhaustive nonexistence theorem.
T4's ten-source corpus and its already-audited generic lacunary results are deliberately not duplicated.
Mutable search responses may change; retained responses and primary PDFs identify exactly what was inspected.
